feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 (span ±0.03) and iteration 1 (span ±0.04) both showed every trial ending off track after exactly one line-loss event, with max_error 0.061 to 0.063 m, progress 0.11 to 0.17 and steering_oscillation 0.08 to 0.16. Widening the span by 2 cm made no measurable difference, so the failure is not explained by span at these widths. Your 10 cm span is the next test. If the next race shows line_loss_events below 1.0 per run and max_error below 0.06 m on the tight bends, keep the span and move on to the drivetrain for progress. If the first loss still occurs at about 0.06 m, span is ruled out and the next change should be the drivetrain. If rms_error rises on gentle bends with the wider span (iteration 1 rms_error about 0.03), the centroid is too coarse, so keep the outer reach and narrow the inner spacing rather than widening further.
requested_changes: Set the outer sensors to x = ±0.05 with inner sensors at ±0.025 (10 cm span, 12 mm footprints), keeping the other geometry unchanged. This is the test of whether the single excursion ends at this span (iterations 0 and 1 showed no change from 6 to 8 cm).

If line_loss_events stays at 1.0 per run with max_error near 0.06 m at the 10 cm span, change wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.10 m, since iterations 0 and 1 had steering_oscillation of only 0.08 to 0.16 and point to a responsiveness limit rather than jitter.

If steering_oscillation rises above the 0.08 to 0.16 range seen in iterations 0 and 1 as tape crosses between sensors, test sensor_size 0.016 m, which overlaps neighbouring sensors and smooths the centroid, and check whether rms_error improves.
